name: fused_dual_quant_hbm_reuse
description: Fuse rowwise + colwise quantisation of the same tensor into one kernel that reads input once. Caveat: L2 cache often hides the second read's HBM cost, so gains are modest on hot paths.
preconditions: Need two different quantisations of the same tensor (e.g. rowwise for fwd, colwise for wgrad in MX-FP8)
Both quantisations can share the same tile shape / scale group size
steps: Single kernel tile reads (BM, BL) of x into registers
Compute both amax paths in-tile: rowwise (along last axis per GROUP) + colwise (along M axis per GROUP)
Produce two fp8 outputs at same (M, L) positions (different scale-applied values)
Write four outputs: fp8_row, scale_row [M, L/32], fp8_col, scale_col [L, total_sc] (jagged)
expected_impact: Measured ~0.1 ms / 1% step gain on cold-L2 single-step runs. Near-zero gain under gradient accumulation where L2 is already warm between back-to-back quant calls. Ship anyway: simpler call graph, no regression, correct-by-construction.
decision_rules: Pursue only if separate quant kernels measurably contend (cold paths, inference-only, large tensor sizes).
MI355X has 4 MB L2 per chiplet + 64 MB MALL — tensors up to ~50 MB stay resident between back-to-back kernel calls.
